lesson.title: America's New Role in the World
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned about US entry into the war. Today: how the war's end reshaped America's global role!

World War I ended in 1918, and the United States emerged from the conflict as a stronger economic and military power on the world stage than it had been before, even though the war caused real hardship and loss. This marked a genuine shift: the US began to play a more active role in global affairs going forward, a change from its earlier, more isolated foreign policy tendencies. Explain why a country emerging from a major war with its industry and military strengthened could see its overall influence in the world grow, even after a costly conflict.
You just learned how the war reshaped America's global role! Tomorrow we'll see the cultural changes that followed at home.

objectives: Understand that the US emerged from WWI with greater global economic/military influence
Explain how a strengthened industry and military can increase a country's overall influence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's US-entry-into-WWI work briefly.
2. Introduce the US's strengthened post-war global position.
3. Have the child explain the industry/military-to-influence connection.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cultural-change lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a simple analogy — a country that comes out of a difficult challenge stronger and better organized than before often finds other countries paying it more attention and respect afterward
Ready for more: ask the child what kinds of decisions a more globally influential country might now be asked to weigh in on that it wasn't before
Kept at a general historical-overview level, continuing this week's chronological thread
teacherGuide.answerKey: A country with strengthened industry and military capacity has more real resources and leverage to influence world events, trade, and diplomacy — other nations tend to take a stronger, more capable country's interests and positions more seriously, which is why the US's post-WWI industrial and military strength translated into greater global influence going forward.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses WA Social Studies and C3 Framework History standards on America's changing role in the world, continuing this week's chronological thread.
